input.question: why haven't we evolved stronger teeth?
input.ground_truth: If our teeth were not good enough to hang in while we bred and raised our young until they were self-sufficient, we would have developed better teeth. Evolutionary adaptations don't happen because it helps us survive. It happens because it helps us live long enough to reproduce and take care of our offspring until *our offspring* can survive. tl;dr: your teeth last until your DNA is done with you.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why haven't we evolved stronger teeth?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your teeth are like the tools you use to eat your favorite crunchy snacks. Over a *long, long* time, our bodies have changed a little bit at a time, but not everything changes super fast.

Our teeth are already strong enough for the kinds of food we eat now. Also, if we get a cavity or lose a tooth, we can go to the dentist and get help. So, our bodies didn’t need to make our teeth even stronger.

Plus, having really, really big or strong teeth might make it hard to talk or smile! So, our teeth are just the right strength for us right now. 🦷😊
